section: Section B: Critical Knowledge — Privacy & Security Literacy
question_type: [Single Choice] Select the best answer based on your privacy persona.

response_options.A: A screen prompting user to enter a one-time code sent to their phone (2-step verification)
response_options.B: A CAPTCHA asking the user to type distorted words
response_options.C: A form asking security questions (e.g., childhood nickname, first manager's name)
response_options.D: A reCAPTCHA grid asking the user to select images containing crosswalks

explanation: 2FA/MFA combines two independent authentication factors — typically 'something you know' (password) and 'something you have' (OTP via SMS/TOTP app). CAPTCHAs and security questions are single-factor mechanisms and do not qualify.
question: Some websites and online services use a security process known as two-step or two-factor authentication. Which of the following images is an example of two-factor authentication?

explanation: Zero-day vulnerabilities are unknown or unpatched flaws that attackers may exploit before a fix is available.
